---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

(forward direction).

The splitting field `L` is **not changed**: along `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'` the same `L` presents the
transported class, via the `K'`-algebra structure `algebraMap K L ∘ e.symm`.  That is where the
`≃` is used and cannot be weakened — for a non-invertible `K → K'` no such structure exists and
one must base-change `L` instead (`exists_witness_of_separable_extension`, a strictly harder
statement).

The four instances about `L/K` are re-derived over `K'`: `Algebra K' L` and
`IsScalarTower k K' L` by `of_algebraMap_eq`, and `Module.Finite K' L`,
`Algebra.IsSeparable K' L` by mathlib's transports along the same commuting square
(`Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv`, `Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv`).  The class equation is
`picEtAffineEquiv_naturality` plus `PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map`, and the witness clause `(W, hW,
hW1)` is carried through **untouched** — it lives over `L`, which did not move. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [Field K'] [Algebra k K'] (e : K ≃ₐ[k] K') (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (h : IsSplitWitness C nu) :
    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom) nu) := by
  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
  letI := hLfield
  letI := hkL
  letI := hKL
  haveI := htow
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hsep
  -- the SAME `L`, now a `K'`-algebra along `e.symm`
  letI hK'L : Algebra K' L := ((algebraMap K L).comp e.symm.toRingHom).toAlgebra
  have halg : ∀ x : K, algebraMap K' L (e x) = algebraMap K L x := fun x => by
    change (algebraMap K L) (e.symm (e x)) = _
    rw [e.symm_apply_apply]
  haveI htow' : IsScalarTower k K' L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
    change algebraMap k L x = (algebraMap K L) (e.symm (algebraMap k K' x))
    rw [show e.symm (algebraMap k K' x) = algebraMap k K x from
      (e.symm.commutes x).trans rfl, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k K L]
  -- the commuting square both mathlib transports are stated against
  have hcomp : ((algebraMap K' L).comp (e.toRingEquiv : K →+* K'))
      = ((RingEquiv.refl L : L →+* L)).comp (algebraMap K L) :=
    RingHom.ext fun x => halg x
  haveI hfin' : Module.Finite K' L :=
    Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv e.toRingEquiv (RingEquiv.refl L) hcomp
  haveI hsep' : Algebra.IsSeparable K' L :=
    Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv e.toRingEquiv (RingEquiv.refl L) hcomp
  refine isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness C _ M ?_ W hW hW1
  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map e.toAlgHom halg]
  exact hM

variable (C) in
/-- **Iso-invariance of `IsSplitWitness`, as an `iff`.**  The reverse direction is the forward
one at `e.symm`, since `overSpecMap` is functorial and `e.symm ∘ e = id`.  An `iff` is what the
locality assembly needs: a one-sided containment would not give openness. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [Field K'] [Algebra k K'] (e : K ≃ₐ[k] K') (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom) nu)
      ↔ IsSplitWitness C nu := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap C e nu⟩
  have hid : Over.overSpecMap (k := k) e.symm.toAlgHom ≫ Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom
      = 𝟙 (overSpec k K) := by
    rw [← Over.overSpecMap_comp, show e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k K from
      AlgHom.ext fun x => e.symm_apply_apply x, Over.overSpecMap_id]
  have hback := isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap C e.symm _ h
  rwa [← picEtMap_comp, hid, picEtMap_id] at hback

variable (C) in
/-- **`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` — DISCHARGED.**

The hypothesis `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest.lean` carries, and the only input standing
between the landed affine openness of `chartLocus` and CHART-U(b) at a general test.  With it,
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` below is unconditional.

The assembly is the naturality square in the slice (`Over.testPoint_comp`): reading the class at
`κ(t)` after restricting along `f` equals restricting along `Spec` of the residue-field
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
-- Constructing and transporting through a field factor of `L ⊗[K] N` needs the larger budget.
/-- A split witness remains a split witness after an arbitrary extension of its reading field.

The output splitting field is not the original one: it is a finite-separable field factor of
the base change of the original field cover.  Consequently no finiteness, separability, or
algebraicity assumption is imposed on the reading-field extension itself.  The auxiliary finite
map `pi` is used only to choose a basic-open cocycle datum through which the `H¹` witness is
transported. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_of_algHom
    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (e : K →ₐ[k] L) (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (h : IsSplitWitness C nu) :
    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e) nu) := by
  obtain ⟨N, hNf, hkN, hKN, htowkKN, hNfin, hNsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
  letI := hNf
  letI := hkN
  letI := hKN
  letI := htowkKN
  letI := hNfin
  letI := hNsep
  letI hKL : Algebra K L := e.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI htowkKL : IsScalarTower k K L :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (e.commutes x).symm
  obtain ⟨P, hPf, hLP, hPfin, hPsep, ⟨q⟩⟩ :=
    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) N).baseChange L).exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
  letI := hPf
  letI := hLP
  letI := hPfin
  letI := hPsep
  letI hkP : Algebra k P := ((algebraMap L P).comp (algebraMap k L)).toAlgebra
  haveI htowkLP : IsScalarTower k L P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  letI hKP : Algebra K P := ((algebraMap L P).comp e.toRingHom).toAlgebra
  haveI htowKLP : IsScalarTower K L P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  haveI htowkKP : IsScalarTower k K P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
    change algebraMap L P (algebraMap k L x) = algebraMap L P (e (algebraMap k K x))
    rw [e.commutes]
  set sigma : N →ₐ[K] P :=
    ((q.restrictScalars K).comp
        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) N).baseChangeInclude L)).comp
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) N).symm.toAlgHom with hsigma
  letI hNP : Algebra N P := sigma.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI htowKNP : IsScalarTower K N P :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (sigma.commutes x).symm
  haveI htowkNP : IsScalarTower k N P := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by

events.text: I found a clean integration theorem: the public rank-one locus is invariant under an isomorphism of field test bases. It composes the existing fieldwise locus characterization with the already-proved `IsSplitWitness` iso-invariance, and introduces no new hypotheses or protected-file edits. I’m adding it as a standalone Picard module and checking it directly.

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    45	
    46	noncomputable section
    47	
    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt
   100	
   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]

   111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
   112	    intro p
   113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
   114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
   115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
   116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
   118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
   119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
   120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
   121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
   122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
   123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
   124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
   125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
   126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
   127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
   128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
   129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
   130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
   131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
   132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
   133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
   134	    exact hs i
   135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
   136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
   137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
   138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
   139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
   140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
   141	      (ht' i)
   142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
   143	
   144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
   145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
   146	consumes. -/
   147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
   148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
   149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

   151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
   152	
   153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
   154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
   155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
   156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
   157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
   158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
   159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
   160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
   161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
   162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
   165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
   166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
   167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
   169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

    27	/-- For the pullback pseudofunctor of over categories, `pullHom` is the literal

    29	lemma pullHom_eq_pullbackFaceIsoOfEq_hom
    30	    {D : Type u} [Category.{v, u} D] [HasPullbacks D]
    31	    {V W X : D} (r₀ r₁ : V ⟶ X) (q : V ⟶ W) (p₀ p₁ : W ⟶ X)
    32	    (J : Over X) (h₀ : r₀ = q ≫ p₀) (h₁ : r₁ = q ≫ p₁)
    33	    (i : (Over.pullback p₀).obj J ≅ (Over.pullback p₁).obj J) :
    34	    pullHom (F := Over.pullbackPseudofunctor (C := D)) i.hom q r₀ r₁ h₀.symm h₁.symm =
    35	      (Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.pullbackFaceIsoOfEq
    36	        r₀ r₁ q p₀ p₁ h₀ h₁ i).hom := by
    37	  subst r₀
    38	  subst r₁
    39	  rfl

     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Comparing raw Pic0 Sigma with its big-etale sheafification
    11	
    12	The raw Pic0 Sigma functor is already a sheaf for the big-etale topology. After the
    13	universe lift required by the Scheme site, the sheafification unit is therefore an
    14	isomorphism. This file bundles that sheaf and records the canonical comparison used by
    15	the quotient-Yoneda step.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    29	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    31	
    32	/-- The universe-raised raw Pic0 Sigma presheaf satisfies the big-etale sheaf
    33	condition in its sieve form. -/
    34	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_ulift_isSheaf_etale :
    35	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology
    36	      (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :=
    37	  Presieve.isSheaf_comp_uliftFunctor Scheme.etaleTopology
    38	    (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf_etale C)
    39	
    40	/-- The universe-raised raw Pic0 Sigma presheaf is a big-etale sheaf. -/
    41	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_ulift_presheafIsSheaf_etale :
    42	    Presheaf.IsSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology
    43	      (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :=
    44	  (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr
    45	    (pic0SigmaFunctor_ulift_isSheaf_etale C)
    46	
    47	/-- The universe-raised raw Pic0 Sigma functor bundled as a big-etale sheaf. -/
    48	noncomputable def pic0SigmaEtaleSheaf :
    49	    Sheaf Scheme.etaleTopology.{u} (Type (u + 1)) :=
    50	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1},
    51	    pic0SigmaFunctor_ulift_presheafIsSheaf_etale C⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The natural isomorphism from universe-raised raw Pic0 Sigma to the underlying
    54	presheaf of the sheafification used as the admissible Abel target. -/
    55	noncomputable def pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso :
    56	    (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) ≅
    57	      (pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification C).obj :=
    58	  isoSheafify Scheme.etaleTopology
    59	    (pic0SigmaFunctor_ulift_presheafIsSheaf_etale C)
    60	
    61	/-- The same canonical comparison bundled in the category of big-etale sheaves. -/
    62	noncomputable def pic0SigmaEtaleSheafIso :
    63	    pic0SigmaEtaleSheaf C ≅ pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification C :=
    64	  sheafificationIso (pic0SigmaEtaleSheaf C)
    65	
    66	/-- The underlying hom of the comparison is exactly the sheafification unit. -/
    67	@[simp]
    68	theorem pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso_hom :
    69	    (pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso C).hom =
    70	      toSheafify Scheme.etaleTopology
    71	        (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :=
    72	  rfl
    73	
    74	/-- The bundled and unbundled comparisons have the same underlying natural map. -/
    75	@[simp]
    76	theorem pic0SigmaEtaleSheafIso_hom :
    77	    (pic0SigmaEtaleSheafIso C).hom.hom =
    78	      (pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso C).hom :=
    79	  rfl
    80	
    81	/-- Component form of the canonical-map identification. -/
    82	@[simp]
    83	theorem pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso_hom_app (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
    84	    (pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso C).hom.app T =
    85	      (toSheafify Scheme.etaleTopology
    86	        (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1})).app T := by
    87	  rw [pic0SigmaEtaleSheafificationIso_hom]
    88	
    89	end
    90	
    91	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeAtBaseField
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingAffineReduction
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Etale-locality of the degree-zero condition
    11	
    12	The degree-zero condition on an affine test is reflected by restriction to a singleton
    13	faithfully flat etale cover.  Given a field point of the base, base-change the cover to that
    14	field and refine it by a finite separable field extension.  The resulting point of the cover
    15	lies above the extended base point.  Degree zero upstairs therefore descends through
    16	`degAt_overSpecMap_eq_zero_iff`.
    17	
    18	This is the degree-condition half of etale descent for `pic0`.  It does not assert effectivity
    19	of descent for the underlying `picEt` class.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    33	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    34	
    35	noncomputable section
    36	
    37	/-- If a Picard class becomes degree zero on a singleton faithfully flat etale cover of an
    38	affine test, then it was already degree zero on the base. -/
    39	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_of_etaleCover
    40	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    41	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A))
    42	    (h : picEtMap C
    43	        (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) lam
    44	      ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :
    45	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) := by
    46	  rw [mem_pic0Subgroup_iff] at h ⊢
    47	  intro K _ _ t
    48	  obtain ⟨phi, rfl⟩ := exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom (k := k) A K t
    49	  letI : Algebra A K := phi.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    50	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A K :=
    51	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (phi.commutes a).symm
    52	  let F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := E.baseChange K
    53	  obtain ⟨L, instFieldL, instAlgebraKL, instFiniteKL, instSeparableKL, ⟨j⟩⟩ :=
    54	    F.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
    55	  letI : Field L := instFieldL
    56	  letI : Algebra K L := instAlgebraKL
    57	  letI : Module.Finite K L := instFiniteKL
    58	  letI : Algebra.IsSeparable K L := instSeparableKL
    59	  letI : Algebra k L :=
    60	    ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
    61	  haveI : IsScalarTower k K L :=
    62	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    63	  let psi : E.Carrier →ₐ[k] L :=
    64	    (j.restrictScalars k).comp ((E.baseChangeInclude K).restrictScalars k)
    65	  let kappa : K →ₐ[k] L := IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K L
    66	  have hcomp :
    67	      psi.comp ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) =
    68	        kappa.comp phi := by
    69	    ext a
    70	    simp only [psi, kappa, AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.restrictScalars_apply,
    71	      Algebra.ofId_apply, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom']
    72	    rw [← j.commutes (phi a)]
    73	    apply congrArg j
    74	    apply (E.baseChangeEquiv K).injective
    75	    unfold Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeInclude
    76	    simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.restrictScalars_apply,
    77	      Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply]
    78	    change (E.baseChangeEquiv K)
    79	        ((E.baseChangeEquiv K).symm
    80	          (1 ⊗ₜ[A] (algebraMap A E.Carrier) a)) =
    81	      (E.baseChangeEquiv K) (algebraMap K F.Carrier (phi a))
    82	    rw [(E.baseChangeEquiv K).apply_symm_apply,
    83	      (E.baseChangeEquiv K).commutes,
    84	      Algebra.TensorProduct.algebraMap_apply]
    85	    convert (TensorProduct.smul_tmul (R := A) a
    86	      (1 : K) (1 : E.Carrier)).symm using 1 <;>
    87	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one,
    88	        RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, RingHom.id_apply]
    89	    exact congrArg (fun x : K => x ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : E.Carrier))
    90	      (congrFun (AlgHom.coe_toRingHom phi) a).symm
    91	  have hzero :
    92	      degAt lam
    93	        (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫
    94	          Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) = 0 := by
    95	    rw [← degAt_picEtMap]
    96	    exact h L (Over.overSpecMap psi)
    97	  have hpoint :
    98	      Over.overSpecMap kappa ≫ Over.overSpecMap phi =
    99	        Over.overSpecMap psi ≫
   100	          Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) := by
   101	    rw [← Over.overSpecMap_comp, ← Over.overSpecMap_comp, hcomp]
   102	  rw [← hpoint] at hzero
   103	  exact (degAt_overSpecMap_eq_zero_iff lam kappa (Over.overSpecMap phi)).mp hzero
   104	
   105	end
   106	
   107	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!

    26	
    27	/-- The tensor-product overlap is the fiber product of `Spec L` with itself over
    28	`Spec k`. -/
    29	lemma tensorOverlap_isPullback : IsPullback
    30	    (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))
    31	    (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))

    43	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := k) (A := L) (B := L)))

    48	/-- The concrete tensor-product overlap, chosen as the pullback used by descent data. -/

    58	
    59	/-- The ring square whose dual is the pullback defining the triple overlap. -/

    61	    IsPushout

    63	        (tensorInr (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    64	      (CommRingCat.ofHom
    65	        (tensorInl (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)

    67	      (CommRingCat.ofHom (Module.descentFace₂₃ k L).toRingHom) := by
    68	  let b : CommRingCat.of k ⟶ CommRingCat.of L :=
    69	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)
    70	  let i₁ : CommRingCat.of L ⟶ CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[k] L) :=
    71	    CommRingCat.ofHom (tensorInl (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom
    72	  let i₂ : CommRingCat.of L ⟶ CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[k] L) :=
    73	    CommRingCat.ofHom (tensorInr (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom
    74	  let f₁₂ : CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶
    75	      CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[k] (L ⊗[k] L)) :=
    76	    CommRingCat.ofHom (Module.descentFace₁₂ k L).toRingHom
    77	  let f₂₃ : CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶
    78	      CommRingCat.of (L ⊗[k] (L ⊗[k] L)) :=

    94	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom
    95	          (R := k) (A := L) (B := L ⊗[k] L)) := by
    96	    ext x

   102	    rfl

   108	    dsimp only [i₁, i₂, f₁₂, f₂₃]

   111	
   112	/-- The two adjacent faces exhibit the triple tensor product as the pullback of

   114	lemma tensorTriple_isPullback : IsPullback
   115	    (tensorTripleFace12 (k := k) (L := L))
   116	    (tensorTripleFace23 (k := k) (L := L))
   117	    (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))
   118	    (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L)) := by
   119	  unfold tensorTripleFace12 tensorTripleFace23 tensorOverlapInr tensorOverlapInl

+
+The public rank-one locus over a field is characterized by `IsSplitWitness`.  The latter is
+invariant under an isomorphism of field extensions, so the locus membership itself is invariant
+under the induced slice isomorphism.  This is a small consumer theorem for the translated-cover
+and descent lanes; it does not assert invariance for arbitrary (non-invertible) field maps.

+    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

    10	/-!
    11	# A finite stage for a rank-one presentation
    12	
    13	The cocycle datum of a rank-one presentation over an arbitrary etale carrier descends to a
    14	finitely generated stage.  Refining once more makes the actual datum-pair `H^1` vanish there.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    19	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    24	open scoped TensorProduct
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    29	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    33	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    34	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    35	
    36	/-- A Noetherian coefficient stage whose datum pulls back to a rank-one presentation datum. -/
    37	structure PicRankOneNoetherianStage
    38	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    39	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    40	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) where
    41	  B0 : Subalgebra k P.cover.Carrier
    42	  hB0fg : B0.FG
    43	  D0 : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (B0 : Type u) pi
    44	  hD0 : D0.baseChange (B' := P.cover.Carrier) = P.datum
    45	  A0 : Subalgebra (B0 : Type u) P.cover.Carrier
    46	  hAnoeth : IsNoetherianRing A0
    47	  hpair : Subsingleton (datumPair (D0.baseChange A0)).H1
    48	  hbase : (D0.baseChange A0).baseChange P.cover.Carrier = P.datum
    49	
    50	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
    51	-- The two nested subalgebra stages carry dependent scalar-tower and datum equalities.
    52	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
    53	/-- A finite Noetherian stage exists for every rank-one presentation. -/
    54	theorem PicRankOneLocalPresentation.nonempty_noetherianStage
    55	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    56	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    57	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    58	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
    59	    Nonempty (PicRankOneNoetherianStage P) := by
    60	  classical
    61	  have hpair : Subsingleton (datumPair P.datum).H1 :=
    62	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing
    63	  obtain ⟨B0, hB0fg, D0, hD0⟩ := P.datum.exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq
    64	  have hpairBase : Subsingleton
    65	      (datumPair (D0.baseChange (B' := P.cover.Carrier))).H1 := by
    66	    rw [hD0]
    67	    exact hpair
    68	  have htensor : Subsingleton ((datumPair D0).H1 ⊗[B0] P.cover.Carrier) :=
    69	    D0.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange P.cover.Carrier hpairBase
    70	  obtain ⟨A0, -, -, hAnoeth, hpairA0, hAA⟩ :=
    71	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_fg_pairH1_vanishing_stage
    72	      (C := C) (pi := pi) B0 hB0fg D0 hpi htensor
    73	  exact ⟨{
    74	    B0 := B0
    75	    hB0fg := hB0fg
    76	    D0 := D0
    77	    hD0 := hD0
    78	    A0 := A0
    79	    hAnoeth := hAnoeth
    80	    hpair := hpairA0
    81	    hbase := hAA.trans hD0 }⟩
    82	
    83	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneNativePresentationDatum
    11	
    12	/-!
    13	# Native rank-one certificates for the lambda-tied datum
    14	
    15	This file closes the Picard-side consumer boundary.  A `PicRankOneNativeDatum` already records
    16	that its etale representative presents the displayed lambda and that its basic-open cocycle datum
    17	represents that same relative Picard class.  Residue-field split witnesses therefore produce the
    18	four cohomological certificates for this exact datum over its arbitrary affine coefficient ring.
    19	
    20	The returned package uses the canonical `h0BaseChange` and `scalarExtension` operations from
    21	`RankOneFamilyCertificates`; `h0BaseChange_tower` proves their coherence along every affine
    22	coefficient tower.  The final constructor passes the package directly to
    23	`PicRankOneNativePresentation.ofCertificates`.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    28	
    29	universe u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    32	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    37	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    38	
    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    40	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    42	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    43	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    44	variable {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    45	
    46	namespace PicRankOneNativeDatum
    47	
    48	/-- The pointwise split condition on the displayed lambda representative carried by `P`. -/
    49	abbrev ResidueSplitWitnesses (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam) : Prop :=
    50	  ∀ t : (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier).left,
    51	    IsSplitWitness C
    52	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
    53	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
    54	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))))
    55	
    56	/-- Produce the complete arbitrary-affine certificate package for the lambda-tied datum `P`.
    57	
    58	The H1 input is converted from split witnesses for `P.representative`; the degree law is derived
    59	from `P.represents` and `P.datum_class`.  Finiteness and projectivity are constructed at a genuine
    60	finite Noetherian stage and transported back, rather than supplied by the caller. -/
    61	noncomputable def familyCertificates
    62	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
    63	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    64	    (hsplit : P.ResidueSplitWitnesses) :
    65	    RankOneFamilyCertificates P.datum :=
    66	  RankOneFamilyCertificates.ofActualDatum P.datum hpi
    67	    (P.residueH1Witness_of_isSplitWitness hsplit)
    68	    (fun L ↦ P.classDeg_baseChange L)
    69	
    70	/-- Canonically extend the lambda-tied certificate package to any affine coefficient algebra. -/
    71	noncomputable def familyCertificatesBaseChange
    72	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
    73	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    74	    (hsplit : P.ResidueSplitWitnesses)
    75	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
    76	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
    77	    RankOneFamilyCertificates (P.datum.baseChange B) :=
    78	  (P.familyCertificates hpi hsplit).scalarExtension B
    79	
    80	end PicRankOneNativeDatum
    81	
    82	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    83	
    84	/-- Assemble a native rank-one presentation from the actual lambda-tied datum and its split
    85	witnesses.  The only remaining independent input is the native pushforward base-change theorem. -/
    86	noncomputable def ofNativeDatum
    87	    (P : PicRankOneNativeDatum pi lam)
    88	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    89	    (hsplit : P.ResidueSplitWitnesses)
    90	    (hpush :
    91	      ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    92	        (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    93	        (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
    94	        (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    95	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g),
    96	        IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.datum.nativeModule)) :
    97	    PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam :=
    98	  PicRankOneNativePresentation.ofCertificates
    99	    P.cover P.representative P.represents P.datum P.datum_class hpush
   100	      (P.familyCertificates hpi hsplit)
   101	
   102	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
   103	
   104	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ThetaShift
    11	
    12	/-!
    13	# The lambda-tied datum underlying a native rank-one presentation
    14	
    15	Every affine Picard value is represented on an etale cover. This file exposes that actual
    16	representative and refines its relative Picard class to a basic-open cocycle datum. The output is
    17	tied to the displayed value; it makes no cohomology, rank, evaluation-divisor, or base-change
    18	claim.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    27	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    32	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    33	
    34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    35	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    37	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    38	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    39	
    40	/--
    41	The part of a native presentation forced by the displayed Picard value.
    42	
    43	`represents` ties the etale-plus representative to `lam`, while `datum_class` ties the
    44	basic-open cocycle datum to that same representative. The geometric certificates that enrich
    45	this datum are intentionally absent.
    46	-/
    47	structure PicRankOneNativeDatum
    48	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    49	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    50	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    51	  represents :
    52	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    53	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    54	  datum_class :
    55	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    56	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    57	
    58	namespace PicRankOneNativeDatum
    59	
    60	/-- Every displayed affine Picard value has a tied basic-open cocycle datum.
    61	
    62	The proof exposes an etale-plus representative of the displayed value, chooses a Cech
    63	representative of its relative Picard class, and refines that class to a basic-open datum.

    16	/-!
    17	# The canonical rank-one divisor, Noetherian-free
    18	
    19	`existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_mem` removes the Noetherian hypothesis from the canonical
    20	rank-one divisor: over any affine test `A` whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus there
    21	is a unique widened locally certified divisor class of degree `genus C` with Abel value the
    22	input class — with no Noetherian hypothesis on any presentation carrier.  The price is the
    23	structural hypothesis `hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom` tying the finite chart to the
    24	curve, which feeds the finite-stage rigid engine.
    25	
    26	Membership tested at the identity yields a presentation `P` of the input class on an étale
    27	carrier `B := P.cover.Carrier`, arbitrary and in general not Noetherian.  The Noetherian
    28	input of the glued-divisor keystone is manufactured by descent:
    29	
    30	* the presented datum descends to a finitely generated — hence Noetherian — stage `A₀` with
    31	  pair-`H¹` vanishing at the stage itself (`exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq` +
    32	  `exists_fg_pairH1_vanishing_stage`);
    33	* stage `H⁰` is finite projective (`datumRigidEngine`), so its `rankAtStalk` is locally
    34	  constant; the rank-one level set of the stage is clopen, contains the image of
    35	  `Spec B → Spec A₀` (rank one over `B` by the presentation), and that image is dense
    36	  because `A₀ ⊆ B` is injective — hence the stage rank is one at every prime;
    37	* rank one at a stage prime gives `h⁰ = 1` on the residue fibre, and the χ-formula
    38	  `h⁰ = deg + (1 − genus)` (`h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi`), solved backwards, pins
    39	  the fibre degree of the stage class at `genus C`; the degree law extends to every field
    40	  point of the stage through the kernel-prime residue embedding
    41	  (`Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ` + `classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`);
    42	* the keystone `exists_glued_divFamZarAff_of_admissible_fibre` now fires at the Noetherian
    43	  stage; the resulting family pushes up to `B`, its Abel value is the restricted input
    44	  class, and `existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_etale_witness` with the discharged
    45	  uniqueness interface descends it uniquely to `A`.
    46	
    47	The unique class is extracted as `canonicalRankOneDivisorOfMem`, with its Abel equation
    48	and uniqueness accessors.
    49	-/

   113	-- The presentation bridge and the fibre H⁰ equivalences elaborate large sheaf terms.
   114	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   115	/-- **Reverse Riemann–Roch at a residue fibre**: for a datum over a Noetherian stage with
   116	vanishing pair-`H¹` and finite projective `H⁰`, stalk rank one at a prime forces the fibre
   117	degree of the datum class at that prime's residue field to be `genus C`.  This inverts the
   118	Σ-RANK1 computation `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one`: there the degree pins the rank; here
   119	`h⁰ = 1` is read off the rank, and the χ-formula `h⁰ = deg + (1 − genus)`
   120	(`h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` through the presentation bridge) is solved for the
   121	degree. -/
   122	private theorem stage_classDeg_residueField
   123	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
   124	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
   125	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1)
   126	    [Module.Finite R (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)]
   127	    [Module.Projective R (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)]
   128	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
   129	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1) :
   130	    classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   131	      (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass)
   132	      = (genus C : ℤ) := by
   133	  rw [← D.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField]
   134	  -- the fibre global-section count is one, inverting the Σ-RANK1 calc
   135	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 := by
   136	    have hcalc : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   137	        = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := by
   138	      calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   139	          = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   140	              (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   141	            Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   142	        _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   143	              (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
   144	            (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
   145	        _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
   146	    rw [← hcalc, hrank]
   147	  -- the χ-formula through the presentation bridge, solved backwards for the degree
   148	  have hsub : Subsingleton
   149	      (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 1) :=
   150	    D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1
   151	  set P : (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).MeromorphicPresentation :=
   152	    Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle
   153	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).pointedCover
   154	      (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).isGluingCocycle
   155	        (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).pointedCover
   156	        (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).pieceIndex
   157	        fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
   158	  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   159	    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv
   160	      (BasicOpenCocycleDatum.presentationSheafIso
   161	        (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   162	      1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp hsub
   163	  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf

   165	    Sheaf.h0_congr (BasicOpenCocycleDatum.presentationSheafIso
   166	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   167	  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi p.asIdeal.ResidueField P hsubP
   168	  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass := rfl
   169	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf
   170	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) = 1 - (genus C : ℤ) :=
   171	    chi_relCurve (chi_moduleKSheaf C) p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   172	  have h1 : ((Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf : ℕ) : ℤ)
   173	      = classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   174	          (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass
   175	        + (1 - (genus C : ℤ)) := by

   184	/-- **The stage degree law at every field point.**  A fibre degree law verified at every
   185	residue field of the stage extends to every field `K` under the stage: the kernel of
   186	`A₀ → K` is a prime `p`, the residue field `κ(p)` embeds in `K` by the universal property
   187	of the residue field (`Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ`), and the degree is invariant under the
   188	base-field transition (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`). -/
   189	private theorem stage_classDeg_field
   190	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   191	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
   192	    (hres : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
   193	      classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   194	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass)
   195	        = (genus C : ℤ))

   197	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K) D.cechPicClass)
   198	      = (genus C : ℤ) := by
   199	  classical
   200	  haveI hker : (RingHom.ker (algebraMap R K)).IsPrime := RingHom.ker_isPrime _
   201	  set p : PrimeSpectrum R := ⟨RingHom.ker (algebraMap R K), hker⟩ with hpdef
   202	  -- the residue field of the kernel prime embeds into `K` over `k`
   203	  have hcompl : p.asIdeal.primeCompl ≤
   204	      (IsUnit.submonoid K).comap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R K) := by
   205	    intro x hx
   206	    rw [Submonoid.mem_comap]
   207	    exact isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr fun h0 => hx (RingHom.mem_ker.mpr h0)
   208	  let rho : p.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[k] K :=
   209	    Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ p.asIdeal (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R K) le_rfl hcompl
   210	  letI : Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField K := rho.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   211	  haveI : IsScalarTower k p.asIdeal.ResidueField K :=
   212	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (rho.commutes x).symm

   214	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x =>
   215	      (Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ_algebraMap p.asIdeal
   216	        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R K) le_rfl hcompl x).symm
   217	  have hcurve : (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap rho).left
   218	      = relCurveMap C p.asIdeal.ResidueField K := by
   219	    refine congrArg
   220	      (fun t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField =>
   221	        (C ◁ t).left) ?_
   222	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   223	  have hinv := classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C rho
   224	    (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass)
   225	  rw [hcurve] at hinv
   226	  calc classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K) D.cechPicClass)
   227	      = classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C p.asIdeal.ResidueField K)
   228	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   229	            D.cechPicClass)) := by
   230	        rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, relCurveMap_comp]
   231	    _ = classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   232	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   233	            D.cechPicClass) := hinv

   236	/-! ## The Noetherian-free canonical divisor -/
   237	
   238	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
   239	-- The stage descent, the clopen-dense rank argument and the keystone application
   240	-- elaborate two localization/subalgebra towers of sheaf terms.
   241	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   242	/-- **The unique Abel-correct divisor of a rank-one class, Noetherian-free**: over any
   243	affine test whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus there is a unique widened locally
   244	certified divisor class of degree `genus C` whose Abel value is the input class.  No
   245	Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on any carrier; the finite-chart normalization `hpi`
   246	replaces it, feeding the finite-stage descent of the presented datum. -/
   247	theorem existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_mem
   248	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   249	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   250	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   251	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A))) :
   252	    ∃! F : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C),
   253	      abelDivAffPlus C A F = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1 := by
   254	  classical
   255	  -- membership tested at the identity yields a presentation of the input class
   256	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mp hlam A (𝟙 (overSpec k A))
   257	  have e : ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map
   258	      (𝟙 (overSpec k A)).op lam).1 = lam.1 :=
   259	    picEtMap_id C lam.1
   260	  -- Step 1: descend the presented datum to a finitely generated Noetherian stage with

    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/

    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/

    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    69	  represents :
    70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi

    74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass

    76	  module_iso :
    77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
    79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module

    81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}

   316	irreducible curve hypotheses.

   319	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)

   422	/-! ## Local-away generators for the canonical evaluation -/
   423	
   424	/-- Nonvanishing on every residue-field fibre of `D(f)` survives passage from the
   425	corresponding prime of the original ring to the residue field of a prime of `A_f`.
   426	
   427	The residue-field comparison is an isomorphism because localization induces bijective
   428	residue-field maps.  Keeping this as a module-level lemma prevents the rank-one
   429	construction from depending on a false definitional transitivity of datum base change. -/
   430	theorem fibre_tmul_ne_zero_of_away
   431	    {A Q : Type u} [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q]
   432	    (f : A) (y : Q)
   433	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   434	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   435	        Q ⊗[A] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   436	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   437	    ((1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] y :
   438	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] Q) ≠ 0 := by
   439	  let p : PrimeSpectrum A :=
   440	    PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) q
   441	  have hfp : f ∉ p.asIdeal := by
   442	    intro hf
   443	    refine q.isPrime.ne_top (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem q.asIdeal
   444	      (Ideal.mem_comap.mp hf) ?_)
   445	    exact IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit f

1	/-

     5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocus
     6	
     7	/-!
     8	# The native module carried by a glued rank-one datum
     9	
    10	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` is already a sheaf of modules over the coefficient
    11	ring.  The presentation contract also asks for the same object as a sheaf of
    12	modules over the structure sheaf of the relative curve.  This file supplies
    13	that bridge: the componentwise `gluedQsmul` action gives a module on every open,
    14	`gluedRes_gluedQsmul` gives the semilinearity needed by
    15	`PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf`, and `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies its
    16	restriction to the coefficient ring with the original datum sheaf.
    17	
    18	The canonical piece trivializations also prove that the native module is a line
    19	bundle.  Pushforward base-change and existence of a tied
    20	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` remain genuine producer obligations.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    32	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    34	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    35	
    36	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    41	
    42	/-- The structure-sheaf module on the sections of the glued datum over one open.
    43	
    44	The action is the componentwise multiplication action; the four module laws
    45	are inherited from the corresponding `gluedQsmul` identities. -/
    46	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleOn (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    47	    Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    48	      ((D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)).obj (op U)) := by
    49	  change Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    50	    (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U))
    51	  letI : SMul Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    52	      (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U)) :=
    53	    ⟨fun r s => gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s⟩
    54	  exact Module.ofMinimalAxioms
    55	    (fun r x y => gluedQsmul_add B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x y)
    56	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_add_left B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    57	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_mul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    58	    (fun x => gluedQsmul_one B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) x)
    59	
    60	/-- The presheaf of structure-sheaf modules underlying `D`. -/
    61	noncomputable def nativePresheaf : (relCurve C B).PresheafOfModules := by
    62	  let M : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
    63	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)
    64	  let family : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    65	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) :=
    66	    fun U => moduleOn D U.unop
    67	  letI : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    68	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) := family
    69	  exact PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf M (by
    70	    intro X Y f r m
    71	    change gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le
    72	        (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : X.unop ≤ X.unop) r m) =
    73	      gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : Y.unop ≤ Y.unop)
    74	        ((relCurve C B).resHom f.unop.le r)
    75	        (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le m)
    76	    rw [gluedRes_gluedQsmul]
    77	    apply Subtype.ext
    78	    funext j
    79	    rw [gluedQsmul_coe, gluedQsmul_coe]
    80	    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom])
    81	
    82	/-- The native `Scheme.Modules` object associated to a glued datum. -/
    83	noncomputable def nativeModule : (relCurve C B).Modules := by
    84	  refine ⟨nativePresheaf D, ?_⟩
    85	  rw [show (nativePresheaf D).presheaf =
    86	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat) from rfl]
    87	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    88	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    89	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    90	    (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} B))).mp D.sheaf.property using 1
    91	  all_goals rfl
    92	
    93	/-! ## Piecewise line-bundle trivializations -/
    94	
    95	/-- Sections of the native module over one cocycle piece are the structure-ring sections.
    96	
    97	The open-immersion ring equivalence transports the component trivialization from the ambient
    98	relative curve to the restricted scheme.  The `gluedTriv_gluedQsmul` identity is exactly the
    99	structure-sheaf semilinearity needed for this to be a linear equivalence over the restricted
   100	ring of sections. -/
   101	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv
   102	    (j : D.index) (V : (D.pieces j).toScheme.Opens) :
   103	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) ≃ₗ[
   104	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) := by
   105	  let e := gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   106	  let ρ := ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   107	  let f : Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) →ₗ[
   108	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) :=
   109	    { toFun := fun s => ρ (e s)
   110	      map_add' := by
   111	        intro s t
   112	        change ρ (e (s + t)) = ρ (e s) + ρ (e t)
   113	        change ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t)) =
   114	          ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s) +
   115	            ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t)
   116	        rw [show gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t) =
   117	            gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s +
   118	              gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t by
   119	              exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).map_add s t]
   120	        exact ρ.map_add _ _
   121	      map_smul' := by
   122	        intro r s
   123	        change ρ
   124	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   125	              (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl) (ρ.symm r) s)) =
   126	          r * ρ
   127	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s)
   128	        rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul]
   129	        simp [ρ] }
   130	  apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective f
   131	  constructor
   132	  · intro s t h
   133	    have h' := congrArg ρ.symm h
   134	    dsimp [f] at h'
   135	    rw [ρ.symm_apply_apply, ρ.symm_apply_apply] at h'
   136	    exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).injective h'
   137	  · intro r
   138	    refine ⟨e.symm (ρ.symm r), ?_⟩
   139	    change ρ (e (e.symm (ρ.symm r))) = r
   140	    rw [e.apply_symm_apply, ρ.apply_symm_apply]
   141	
   142	/-- The piecewise section equivalences assemble to a sheaf isomorphism with the unit module. -/
   143	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSheafIso (j : D.index) :
   144	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D) ≅
   145	      SheafOfModules.unit (D.pieces j).toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
   146	  (SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _).preimageIso
   147	    (PresheafOfModules.isoMk
   148	      (fun V => (nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv D j V.unop).toModuleIso)
   149	      (fun {V W} f => by
   150	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   151	        apply LinearMap.ext
   152	        intro x
   153	        change
   154	          ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso W.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   155	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le W.unop)
   156	                (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit
   157	                  ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop)) x)) =
   158	            (D.pieces j).toScheme.presheaf.map f
   159	              (((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   160	                (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x))
   161	        rw [gluedTriv_res B D.isGluingCocycle j
   162	          ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   163	          ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x]
   164	        simp only [Scheme.Opens.ι_appIso]
   165	        change
   166	          (relCurve C B).resHom
   167	              ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   168	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   169	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x) =
   170	            (relCurve C B).presheaf.map
   171	              ((D.pieces j).ι.opensFunctor.map f.unop).op
   172	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   173	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x)
   174	        rfl))
   175	
   176	/-- The canonical native module is locally a free rank-one structure-sheaf module. -/
   177	theorem nativeModule_isLineBundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle (nativeModule D) := by
   178	  intro x
   179	  let j := D.pieceIndex x
   180	  refine ⟨D.pieces j, D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex x, ?_⟩
   181	  exact ⟨nativeModulePieceSheafIso D j⟩
   182	
   183	/-- On every open, restricting `D.nativeModule` to the coefficient ring recovers
   184	the datum's original module of sections.
   185	
   186	The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive
   187	point: `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies the native structure-sheaf action
   188	of a coefficient scalar with the datum's coefficient action. -/
   189	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv
   190	    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
   191	    (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   192	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) ≃ₗ[B]
   193	      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by
   194	  let f :
   195	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   196	        (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[B]
   197	        D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) :=
   198	    { toFun := fun x => x
   199	      map_add' := by
   200	        intros
   201	        rfl
   202	      map_smul' := by
   203	        intro r x
   204	        change gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U)
   205	            ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B U r) x =
   206	          r • (show D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) from x)
   207	        exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap B D.pieces D.unit
   208	          (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x }
   209	  exact LinearEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun y => ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩
   210	
   211	/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.
   212	
   213	This has exactly the type of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.module_iso` when the
   214	presentation's native module is chosen to be `D.nativeModule`. -/
   215	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSheafIso :
   216	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   217	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D) ≅ D.sheaf :=
   218	  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimageIso
   219	    (NatIso.ofComponents
   220	      (fun U => (nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv D U.unop).toModuleIso)
   221	      (fun {_ _} _ => by
   222	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   223	        apply LinearMap.ext
   224	        intro x
   225	        rfl))
   226	
   227	end
   228	
   229	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

    12	/-!
    13	# Native presentations for split field classes
    14	
    15	A residue-field H¹ witness for the lambda-tied cocycle datum supplies its arbitrary-ring
    16	cohomology and rank certificates.  The native all-cartesian base-change theorem then completes
    17	the corresponding `PicRankOneNativePresentation` without a separate pushforward hypothesis.
    18	
    19	A split genus-degree class over a field stays split after every affine coefficient extension,

    30

   630	theorem sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero

   645	      ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y) :

   664	/-- A rank-one presentation has a tied local-away evaluation generator.
   665	
   666	The rank-one field of `P` makes every residue-field fibre of its `H⁰` module nontrivial.
   667	The projective-module generator lemma therefore supplies a single basic open `D(f)` and
   668	one datum section `y` which stays nonzero on every residue fibre over that open.  The same
   669	`y` is transported to a native global section and its unit-lift through the evaluation
   670	counit; the final conjunct records that counit identity explicitly so the future
   671	`divisorOfRankOne` construction consumes this witness rather than an unrelated section.
   672	-/
   673	theorem exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator
   674	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   675	    (p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier) :
   676	    ∃ f : P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   677	      ∃ y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0,
   678	        (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ q.asIdeal →
   679	          (y ⊗ₜ (1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   680	            Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   681	              q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) ∧
   682	        (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
   683	          ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   684	            (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
   685	          (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := by
   686	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0
   687	  letI : Module.Finite P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_finite
   688	  letI : Module.Projective P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_projective
   689	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   690	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) = 1 := by
   691	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   692	    exact P.h0_rank_one p
   693	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) :=
   694	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   695	  haveI : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   696	    (TensorProduct.comm P.cover.Carrier _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   697	  obtain ⟨f, hf, y, hy⟩ :=
   698	    Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p (Q := Q)
   699	      (by infer_instance)
   700	  refine ⟨f, hf, y, ?_, ?_⟩
   701	  · simpa only [Q] using hy
   702	  · exact P.evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 y

   706	The nonvanishing proof is derived by
   707	`sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero`; it is not additional witness data.
   708	Together with `exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator`, this is the immediate local divisor
   709	consumer on the datum side.  Identifying it with the native evaluation zero locus remains
   710	a separate `O`-module base-change contract. -/
   711	noncomputable def baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations
   712	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   713	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   714	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)

   730	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
